12/// PdfCraft patch: index entries read from one object stream (the same clamp `pdfcraft_cos`
13/// applies to `/N`). Entries past it are ignored, so a huge index block cannot allocate an entry
14/// list or parse a member per entry.
15pub(crate) const MAX_OBJECT_STREAM_MEMBERS: usize = 1_000_000;
16
17/// PdfCraft patch: objects (every member and everything nested in it) one load may build from
18/// all of its object streams together, about one per object of the largest cross-reference
19/// table `pdfcraft_cos` accepts (8,388,607). Each stream is bounded by the decompression limit,
20/// but a file may hold many, and every two decoded bytes can be an object of a hundred bytes or
21/// more; this keeps the worst case near a gigabyte instead of tens.
22pub(crate) const MAX_LOAD_NODES: usize = 1 << 23;
23
24/// PdfCraft patch: the objects parsing may still build, shared by every object stream one load
25/// parses (and by rayon workers, hence atomic). Each member reserves its share before parsing
26/// and refunds what it did not use, so concurrent members cannot overshoot the total. Public so
27/// PdfCraft's tests can load object streams from a small budget.
28///
29/// The loaders parse their object streams one after another in object-number order, and a
30/// stream whose members could run the budget out parses them in index order (see
31/// [`ObjectStream::new_within`]), so the members skipped once it is spent are the same on every
32/// load of a file.
33pub struct NodeBudget(AtomicUsize);
34
35impl NodeBudget {
36    /// A budget of `nodes` objects.
37    pub fn new(nodes: usize) -> Self {
38        Self(AtomicUsize::new(nodes))
39    }
40
41    /// Take up to `want` nodes and return how many were granted (0 once the budget is spent).
42    fn reserve(&self, want: usize) -> usize {
43        // A compare-exchange loop rather than `fetch_update`, which newer toolchains deprecate
44        // in favour of a `try_update` older than this crate's minimum Rust version.
45        let mut left = self.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
46        loop {
47            let take = left.min(want);
48            match self.0.compare_exchange_weak(left, left - take, Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed) {
49                Ok(_) => return take,
50                Err(now) => left = now,
51            }
52        }
53    }
54
55    /// Give back nodes [`Self::reserve`] granted and parsing did not use. Refunds never exceed
56    /// what was taken, so the count stays within the starting budget and cannot overflow.
57    fn refund(&self, nodes: usize) {
58        self.0.fetch_add(nodes, Ordering::Relaxed);
59    }
60
61    /// The nodes not yet reserved.
62    fn left(&self) -> usize {
63        self.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
64    }
65
66    /// Whether nothing is left to build from.
67    pub fn spent(&self) -> bool {
68        self.left() == 0
69    }
70}

97impl ObjectStream {
98    /// Parse an existing object stream without modifying its encoded content or
99    /// filter dictionary.
100    ///
101    /// This decodes the stream without any size limit. For untrusted input,
102    /// prefer [`ObjectStream::new_with_limit`] to guard against decompression
103    /// bombs.
104    pub fn new(stream: &Stream) -> Result<ObjectStream> {
105        Self::new_with_limit(stream, None)
106    }
107
108    /// Parse an existing object stream without modifying it, rejecting the
109    /// decoded content if it would exceed `max_decompressed_size` bytes. `None`
110    /// means no limit (the behavior of [`ObjectStream::new`]).
111    ///
112    /// PdfCraft patch: members are built from a budget of `MAX_LOAD_NODES` objects of their own.
113    pub fn new_with_limit(stream: &Stream, max_decompressed_size: Option<usize>) -> Result<ObjectStream> {
114        Self::new_within(stream, max_decompressed_size, &NodeBudget::new(MAX_LOAD_NODES))
115    }
116
117    /// PdfCraft patch: [`ObjectStream::new_with_limit`], building members from `budget`, which a
118    /// load shares between all of its object streams. A member that would exceed its share, or
119    /// any member once the budget is spent, is skipped with a warning.
120    ///
121    /// When the budget holds enough for every member, they are parsed in parallel from a share
122    /// reserved for this stream alone, which no member can run out; otherwise they are parsed in
123    /// index order from `budget`. Either way which members are built doesn't depend on the order
124    /// in which rayon's workers reach them.
125    pub fn new_within(stream: &Stream, max_decompressed_size: Option<usize>, budget: &NodeBudget) -> Result<ObjectStream> {
126        Self::new_members_within(stream, max_decompressed_size, budget, |_| true)
127    }
128
129    /// PdfCraft patch: [`ObjectStream::new_within`], parsing only the members whose object
130    /// number `keep` accepts. The others are never parsed, so they spend nothing from `budget`:
131    /// a loader passes the members it would add (not placed in another stream by the
132    /// cross-reference table, and not already loaded), and a lookup the one member it wants.
133    pub(crate) fn new_members_within(
134        stream: &Stream,
135        max_decompressed_size: Option<usize>,
136        budget: &NodeBudget,
137        keep: impl Fn(u32) -> bool,
138    ) -> Result<ObjectStream> {
139        let content = match max_decompressed_size {
140            // Object streams are decoded while the document is loaded, so
141            // enforcing the limit here bounds the memory a single stream can use.
142            Some(max) => stream.get_plain_content_with_limit(max)?,
143            None => stream.get_plain_content()?,
144        };
145
146        if content.is_empty() {
147            return Ok(ObjectStream { objects: BTreeMap::new(), max_objects: 100, compression_level: 6 });
148        }
149
150        let first_offset =
151            stream.dict.get(b"First").and_then(Object::as_i64)?.try_into().map_err(|e: TryFromIntError| Error::NumericCast(e.to_string()))?;
152        let index_block = content.get(..first_offset).ok_or(Error::InvalidOffset(first_offset))?;
153
154        let numbers_str = std::str::from_utf8(index_block).map_err(|e| Error::InvalidObjectStream(e.to_string()))?;
155        // PdfCraft patch: read at most `MAX_OBJECT_STREAM_MEMBERS` index entries.
156        let numbers: Vec<_> = numbers_str.split_whitespace().take(2 * MAX_OBJECT_STREAM_MEMBERS).map(|number| u32::from_str(number).ok()).collect();
157        let len = numbers.len() / 2 * 2; // Ensure only pairs.
158
159        let n = stream.dict.get(b"N").and_then(Object::as_i64)?;
160        if numbers.len().try_into().ok() != n.checked_mul(2) {
161            warn!("object stream: the object stream dictionary specifies a wrong number of objects")
162        }
163        if usize::try_from(n).is_ok_and(|n| n > MAX_OBJECT_STREAM_MEMBERS) {
164            warn!("object stream: /N {n} exceeds {MAX_OBJECT_STREAM_MEMBERS}; later members are ignored")
165        }
166
167        // PdfCraft patch: bound members by the next distinct offset and parse each offset
168        // only once, so overlapping or duplicate entries cannot amplify decoded content.
169        let mut extents = BTreeMap::new();
170        for (index, chunk) in numbers[..len].chunks(2).enumerate() {
171            if let &[Some(_), Some(offset)] = chunk {
172                let offset = first_offset.saturating_add(offset as usize);
173                if offset < content.len() {
174                    extents.entry(offset).or_insert((index, content.len()));
175                }
176            }
177        }
178        let mut end = content.len();
179        for (&offset, (_, extent_end)) in extents.iter_mut().rev() {
180            *extent_end = end;
181            end = offset;
182        }
183
184        // PdfCraft patch: find each member's bytes first, in index order, so the members can be
185        // charged to the budget before any is parsed.
186        let mut members = Vec::new();
187        for (index, chunk) in numbers[..len].chunks(2).enumerate() {
188            let &[Some(id), Some(offset)] = chunk else { continue };
189            let offset = first_offset.saturating_add(offset as usize);
190
191            if offset >= content.len() {
192                warn!("out-of-bounds offset in object stream");
193                continue;
194            }
195            let Some(&(first_index, extent_end)) = extents.get(&offset) else {
196                continue;
197            };
198            if index != first_index {
199                warn!("duplicate offset in object stream");
200                continue;
201            }
202            if !keep(id) {
203                continue;
204            }
205            // Skip leading whitespace — some PDFs emit newlines before objects in ObjStm
206            let mut start = offset;
207            while start < extent_end && content.get(start).is_some_and(u8::is_ascii_whitespace) {
208                start += 1;
209            }
210            if start >= extent_end {
211                warn!("only whitespace after offset in object stream");
212                continue;
213            }
214            members.push((id, start, extent_end));
215        }
216
217        // PdfCraft patch: each member builds at most `MAX_OBJECT_NODES` objects, reserved from
218        // `from`; once that is spent the remaining members are skipped unparsed. Every object
219        // takes at least one byte, so a member reserves no more than its length.
220        let share = |&(_, start, end): &(u32, usize, usize)| parser::MAX_OBJECT_NODES.min(end - start);
221        let skipped = AtomicBool::new(false);
222        let parse_member = |from: &NodeBudget, member: &(u32, usize, usize)| -> Option<(ObjectId, Object)> {
223            let &(id, start, end) = member;
224            let granted = from.reserve(share(member));
225            if granted == 0 {
226                skipped.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
227                return None;
228            }
229            let nodes = Cell::new(granted);
230            let object = content.get(start..end).and_then(|bytes| parser::direct_object_within(bytes, &nodes));
231            from.refund(nodes.get());
232            if object.is_none() && nodes.get() == 0 {
233                warn!("object stream: member {id} exceeds the object budget and was skipped");
234            }
235            Some(((id, 0), object?))
236        };
237
238        let want = members.iter().map(&share).fold(0, usize::saturating_add);
239        let granted = budget.reserve(want);
240        let objects: BTreeMap<ObjectId, Object> = if granted == want {
241            // Every member fits, so they are parsed in parallel from this stream's own share:
242            // its members' reservations add up to it, so none is refused whatever the order.
243            let own = NodeBudget::new(granted);
244            let objects = members.par_iter().filter_map(|member| parse_member(&own, member)).collect();
245            #[cfg(any())]
246            let objects = members.iter().filter_map(|member| parse_member(&own, member)).collect();
247            budget.refund(own.left());
248            objects
249        } else {
250            // The budget may run out part-way, so the members are parsed in index order and the
251            // ones skipped are the same on every load.
252            budget.refund(granted);
253            members.iter().filter_map(|member| parse_member(budget, member)).collect()
254        };
255        if skipped.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
256            warn!("object stream: the object budget is spent; remaining members were skipped");
257        }
258
259        Ok(ObjectStream { objects, max_objects: 100, compression_level: 6 })
260    }
261
262    /// Create a builder for constructing new object streams
263    pub fn builder() -> ObjectStreamBuilder {
264        ObjectStreamBuilder { max_objects: 100, compression_level: 6 }
265    }
266
267    /// Add an object to the stream
268    pub fn add_object(&mut self, id: ObjectId, obj: Object) -> Result<()> {
269        // Check if object can be added to stream
270        if matches!(obj, Object::Stream(_)) {
271            return Err(Error::InvalidObjectStream("Stream objects cannot be stored in object streams".into()));
272        }
273
274        // Check capacity
275        if self.objects.len() >= self.max_objects {
276            return Err(Error::InvalidObjectStream(format!("Object stream has reached maximum capacity of {} objects", self.max_objects)));
277        }
278
279        self.objects.insert(id, obj);
280        Ok(())
281    }
282
283    /// Get the number of objects in the stream
284    pub fn object_count(&self) -> usize {
285        self.objects.len()
286    }
287
288    /// Build the stream content in the format required by PDF spec
289    pub fn build_stream_content(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
290        if self.objects.is_empty() {
291            return Ok(Vec::new());
292        }
293
294        // Sort objects by ID for consistent output
295        let mut sorted_objects: Vec<_> = self.objects.iter().collect();
296        sorted_objects.sort_by_key(|(id, _)| *id);
297
298        // First build the offset table to know its size
299        let mut offset_entries = Vec::new();
300        let mut current_offset = 0;
301
302        for ((obj_num, _gen), obj) in &sorted_objects {
303            // Store the object number and its offset
304            offset_entries.push(format!("{obj_num} {current_offset}"));
305
306            // Calculate size of this object's serialization
307            let mut obj_bytes = Vec::new();
308            crate::third_party::lopdf::writer::Writer::write_object(&mut obj_bytes, obj)?;
309            current_offset += obj_bytes.len() + 1; // +1 for space separator
310        }
311
312        // Build the complete offset table with proper spacing
313        let offset_table = offset_entries.join(" ") + " ";
314
315        // Now build the final content
316        let mut content = Vec::new();
317        content.extend_from_slice(offset_table.as_bytes());
318
319        // Add serialized objects with space separators
320        for ((_, _), obj) in &sorted_objects {
321            let mut obj_bytes = Vec::new();
322            crate::third_party::lopdf::writer::Writer::write_object(&mut obj_bytes, obj)?;
323            content.extend_from_slice(&obj_bytes);
324            content.push(b' '); // Space separator between objects
325        }
326
327        Ok(content)
328    }
329
330    /// Convert to a Stream object ready for insertion into a PDF
331    pub fn to_stream_object(&self) -> Result<Stream> {
332        let content = self.build_stream_content()?;
333
334        // Calculate where the first object starts
335        // We need to find the size of the offset table
336        let mut sorted_objects: Vec<_> = self.objects.iter().collect();
337        sorted_objects.sort_by_key(|(id, _)| *id);
338
339        // Build the offset entries to calculate exact size
340        let mut offset_entries = Vec::new();
341        let mut current_offset = 0;
342
343        for ((obj_num, _gen), obj) in &sorted_objects {
344            offset_entries.push(format!("{obj_num} {current_offset}"));
345
346            // Calculate size of this object's serialization
347            let mut obj_bytes = Vec::new();
348            crate::third_party::lopdf::writer::Writer::write_object(&mut obj_bytes, obj)?;
349            current_offset += obj_bytes.len() + 1; // +1 for space separator
350        }
351
352        // The offset table is joined with spaces and has a trailing space
353        let offset_table = offset_entries.join(" ") + " ";
354        let first_offset = offset_table.len();
355
356        let dict = dictionary! {
357            "Type" => "ObjStm",
358            "N" => self.objects.len() as i64,
359            "First" => first_offset as i64,
360        };
361
362        let mut stream = Stream::new(dict, content);
363
364        // Apply compression - object streams should always be compressed
365        if self.compression_level > 0 {
366            // Force compression by setting Filter directly
367            use flate2::Compression;
368            use flate2::write::ZlibEncoder;
369            use std::io::prelude::*;
370
371            let compression = match self.compression_level {
372                0 => Compression::none(),
373                1..=3 => Compression::fast(),
374                4..=6 => Compression::default(),
375                _ => Compression::best(),
376            };
377
378            let mut encoder = ZlibEncoder::new(Vec::new(), compression);
379            encoder.write_all(&stream.content)?;
380            let compressed = encoder.finish()?;
381
382            stream.dict.set("Filter", "FlateDecode");
383            stream.set_content(compressed);
384        }
385
386        Ok(stream)
387    }

389    /// Check if an object can be compressed into an object stream
390    pub fn can_be_compressed(id: ObjectId, obj: &Object, doc: &Document) -> bool {
391        // Rule 1: Stream objects cannot be compressed
392        if matches!(obj, Object::Stream(_)) {
393            return false;
394        }
395
396        // Rule 2: Objects with non-zero generation cannot be compressed
397        if id.1 != 0 {
398            return false;
399        }
400
401        // Rule 3: Only encryption dictionary cannot be compressed from trailer references
402        if let Ok(Object::Reference(encrypt_ref)) = doc.trailer.get(b"Encrypt")
403            && id == *encrypt_ref
404        {
405            return false;
406        }
407
408        // Rule 4: Specific object types that cannot be compressed
409        if let Object::Dictionary(dict) = obj
410            && let Ok(type_obj) = dict.get(b"Type")
411            && let Ok(type_name) = type_obj.as_name()
412        {
413            match type_name {
414                // Cross-reference streams and object streams cannot be compressed
415                b"XRef" => return false,
416                b"ObjStm" => return false,
417
418                // Catalog can only be excluded in linearized PDFs
419                b"Catalog" if Self::is_linearized(doc) => {
420                    return false;
421                }
422                b"Catalog" => {}
423
424                // Page, Pages, and all other types CAN be compressed
425                _ => {}
426            }
427        }
428
429        // Default: Allow compression
430        true
431    }
432
433    /// Check if a PDF document is linearized
434    fn is_linearized(doc: &Document) -> bool {
435        // In a linearized PDF, the first object after the header should be a
436        // linearization dictionary with /Linearized entry
437        // For simplicity, we check if any object has a /Linearized entry
438        for obj in doc.objects.values() {
439            if let Object::Dictionary(dict) = obj
440                && dict.has(b"Linearized")
441            {
442                return true;
443            }
444        }
445        false
446    }

449impl ObjectStreamBuilder {
450    /// Set the maximum number of objects per stream
451    pub fn max_objects(mut self, max: usize) -> Self {
452        self.max_objects = max;
453        self
454    }
455
456    /// Set the compression level (0-9)
457    pub fn compression_level(mut self, level: u32) -> Self {
458        self.compression_level = level;
459        self
460    }
461
462    /// Build the ObjectStream
463    pub fn build(self) -> ObjectStream {
464        ObjectStream { objects: BTreeMap::new(), max_objects: self.max_objects, compression_level: self.compression_level }
465    }
466
467    /// Get the current max_objects setting
468    pub fn get_max_objects(&self) -> usize {
469        self.max_objects
470    }
471
472    /// Get the current compression_level setting

474        self.compression_level
